transcript.text: Bosch WAJ28001GB washing machine just beeps and shows E17 a few minutes into every wash. Drum hardly has any water in it. What's E17?

I can't confirm the exact definition for your specific model, but on Bosch washing machines E17 most likely means a water supply or fill timeout. The machine has tried to fill to its working level and hasn't got there within the allowed time, so it stops and beeps. That fits with the drum having hardly any water in it. 1. Water isn't getting in fast enough. The tap may be partly closed, the inlet hose may be kinked or squashed behind the machine, or the small mesh filter where the hose screws onto the machine may be blocked with grit or limescale. This is the most common cause.
2. Water is getting in but escaping down the drain as fast as it fills. This is called siphoning. It usually happens when the drain hose sits too low or is pushed too far down the standpipe.
3. The inlet valve on the machine is failing and only lets a trickle through, or none at all.
4. Less often, low mains pressure or a restricted (or, in cold weather, frozen) supply pipe. 1. Find the machine's water tap, usually a blue-handled lever under the sink or behind the machine. Make sure it's fully open, with the lever in line with the pipe. Pull the machine out gently and check the inlet hose isn't kinked or crushed. If either was the problem, run a rinse and see whether the E17 clears.
2. Check the inlet filter. Switch off and unplug the machine, turn the tap off and put a towel down. Unscrew the inlet hose from the back of the machine and look inside the connection for a small mesh filter. If it's clogged, pull it out carefully with pliers, rinse it under the tap and refit it. Also look at the tap end of the hose. Before reconnecting, hold the hose over a bucket and briefly open the tap. A strong flow means your supply is fine, and the problem is the machine. A weak flow points to the tap or pipework.
3. Check the drain hose. It should rise in a hook to at least about 60 cm above the floor before going into the standpipe or sink trap, and only a few centimetres of it should be inside the standpipe. If it's lying low or pushed right down, water can siphon away during the fill. 4. Check the pressure elsewhere. Run the cold tap nearest the machine. If it's weak too, the problem is the household supply rather than the machine. If the tap, hose, filter a

The little lever on the pipe behind the machine was at an angle, about half way. I think the plumber must have knocked it when he fitted the new kitchen tap on Monday. I turned it in line with the pipe so it's fully open, then ran a rinse. It filled quickly, there was no E17, and the rinse finished. The hose isn't kinked and the kitchen cold tap flows normally. I haven't checked the drain hose, and I'd rather not take the inlet filter off unless I need to. There's no water on the floor and no smells.

That's sorted, then. The half-closed tap is probably the whole story. With the lever at an angle the machine couldn't fill to its working level in the time it allows, so it stopped with E17. Now that it fills quickly and finishes a rinse with no code, there's no need to touch the inlet filter or the drain hose. Siphoning or a blocked filter wouldn't have cleared just by opening the tap. One tip for the future: whenever anyone works under the sink or behind the machine, glance at that lever afterwards. It should sit in line with the pipe. Many people put a bit of tape or a marker by it as a reminder. If E17 ever comes back with the tap fully open, the next things to look at are the small mesh filter where the hose meets the machine, then the drain hose height. For now, though, it should be fine. Is there anything else I can help with?

claimsRejected.claim: In that case you'd often hear water running out while it's filling.

candidates: Restricted water supply: tap part-closed, kinked inlet hose or blocked inlet hose filter (high)
Water siphoning out down the drain hose as it fills (drain hose too low or pushed too far into the standpipe) (medium)
Faulty inlet valve (not opening or only partly opening) (medium)
Low household water pressure or a frozen or restricted supply pipe (low)

reading.symptom: beeps and shows E17 a few minutes into every wash

plan: They asked: "What's E17?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model WAJ28001GB; code E17.
The fault they reported is: "beeps and shows E17 a few minutes into every wash". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Isolation tap left half closed after plumbing work, restricting the fill (high)

reading.symptom: E17 fill timeout, drum hardly filling

tags.checkGiven: Check the tap the fill hose connects to is turned fully on, and that the hose behind the machine isn't kinked or squashed against the wall.

plan: The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.
